evidence.description: REQ-115's canonical 9-step order is directly traceable in executeLoanIssuanceAttempt/runLockedIssuance: step 1 self-loan check (line 270), step 2 co-location (line 281-286), step 3 pre-lock kill-switch (line 288-293), step 4 nested dual-lock acquisition via resolveLoanLockAcquisitionOrder (line 297-302), step 5 resolveStaleProvisioning/reconciliation (line 182-187), step 6 fresh recheck of isBorrowerEligible+kill-switches (line 189-208), step 7 sizing via computeLoanCapUsd/computeLenderAvailableUsd/decideLoan (line 210-221), step 8 nextLoanSequenceForLender + provisional append (line 223-237), step 9 disburse try/catch + follow-up append (line 239-258). No step reordered, no step skipped.

REQ-116's two entry points match spec exactly: executeRepaymentClaim acquires loan_${loanId} lock, rejects a non-active last row BEFORE calling verify (line 325-327), calls verifyRepayment with expectedFrom=borrower_wallet/expectedTo=lender_wallet (correct repay direction), appends the status-transition row only on a genuine credit. executeDefaultDetectionSweep reads candidates from detectDefaultedLoans directly (line 369), loops sequentially (never Promise.all) with a fresh per-candidate re-read before appending (line 379-393), skips a lock-held candidate without blocking (line 394).

Every imported function's call-site signature was independently checked against lending-gate.mjs/lending-verify.mjs's own exported signatures (isBorrowerEligible, computeLenderAvailableUsd, sumRecentGojoGiftsUsd's positional (gojoLogRows,nowMs,lookbackHours,lenderId) order, verifyRepayment, reconcileProvisionalDisbursement, resolveLoanLockAcquisitionOrder, nextLoanSequenceForLender) -- all match exactly, no argument-order or field-name mismatch found. payViaFacilitator's real return shape ({ok,tx,payer,...}, escrow.mjs:139) matches activeStatusFields(disburseResult.tx, nowMs)'s own usage.

Independently re-run (not accepted from any prior log): `cd ~/anicca && node --test skills/economy/lending/lib/__tests__/*.test.mjs` -> 120/120 pass, 0 fail. Re-ran lending-orchestrator.test.mjs alone 3 additional times (31/31 each run) to check for the flakiness the contract's own Phase 2c note described around the sweep-vs-claim yield fix -- zero flakiness observed across all runs.

FIND-C203 fix independently confirmed present: 'PROP-115c step 7 (sizing computation refuses...)' test exists, asserts reason 'insufficient_lender_surplus', zero rows, both locks released -- closes the previously-missing step-7 sizing-refusal coverage the contract's own round-1 review found missing.

Adversary-written standalone probe beyond the existing test suite, per the manifest's explicit ask ('could executeDefaultDetectionSweep's own per-candidate loop ever race against ITSELF'): two concurrent executeDefaultDetectionSweep({nowMs}) calls fired via Promise.all against ONE shared ledger with 8 simultaneously-overdue candidates for the SAME lender. Executed 5 times. Every run: all 8 candidates end up defaulted exactly once (union of both sweeps' own defaulted[] return arrays = 8, intersection = 0 -- the two sweeps never both claim the same loan_id), zero loan_id ever received more than one 'defaulted' row append. Confirms the per-loan-id lock (loan.mjs's real, atomic fs.open(wx)-based withGigLock, fail-closed/never-queued) plus each candidate's own fresh re-read (line 380-381) genuinely prevents a sweep from racing against itself, not merely against executeRepaymentClaim, under REAL concurrent execution (never a mocked lock).

Independent code read confirms the two-phase provisional/follow-up discipline cannot double-record or lose a loan within one call: step 9 is a single try/catch with three mutually-exclusive branches (catch->disbursement_uncertain, ok!==true->disbursement_failed, success->active), each returning immediately after exactly one follow-up append -- no code path appends twice or falls through without appending. A provisioning/disbursement_uncertain row left by a prior failed attempt is picked up by the NEXT issuance attempt for the same lender via resolveStaleProvisioning's ledger-state-triggered reconciliation (step 5, line 103-120), which reads the highest-n row's status before any new sequence number is computed -- confirmed both by source read and by the passing 'PROP-115c step 5 happy' test (line 337-364), which asserts the new attempt's own n=2 is computed strictly after n=1's reconciliation resolves.

Independently read settleBody (payViaFacilitator's own implementation) to confirm its real return shape on success is {ok:true, tx, payer} -- matches lending-orchestrator.mjs:257's own activeStatusFields(disburseResult.tx, nowMs) usage exactly; on any of the three failure stages (verify/settle/confirm) it returns {ok:false, stage, reason, raw} -- matches the orchestrator's own `disburseResult.ok !== true` failure-path check (line 249).

Independently read withGigLock's real implementation: POSIX-atomic fs.open(file,'wx') primary acquisition, atomic fs.rename-based stale reclaim, fail-closed (never queues -- a caller that cannot acquire immediately returns {ok:false} without ever calling fn()). This confirms the orchestrator's own lock_held handling (executeLoanIssuanceAttempt line 305-307, checking lockResult.ok===false from either the outer or inner nested withGigLock call) correctly covers both the outer-acquisition-fails and inner-acquisition-fails cases -- in both, runLockedIssuance (which performs all appends) is never invoked, so zero partial-lock/partial-append leak is structurally possible.

CRIT-206/FIND-C202 correction independently re-verified: PROP-025 (artifact specs/verification-architecture.md#PROP-108a) is status:'skipped', required:false in the CURRENT state.json -- matches the contract's own stated correction (the stale 'proved via a borrowed sprint-1 fixture-only harness with zero orchestrator involvement' entry was fixed, never re-introduced). No artifact anywhere in this sprint's diff claims PROP-108a proved via a fixture/simulated transfer/borrowed artifact.

Confirmed via `git diff <pre-sprint-2 commit>..HEAD -- lending-gate.mjs lending-verify.mjs gojo-read.mjs lending-path.mjs` that all 4 sprint-1-delivered files are byte-identical (zero diff lines) to their sprint-1 content -- CRIT-201's 'no incidental edits' clause holds. Their own pre-existing 89 tests all still pass unmodified as part of the 120/120 full-suite run.

Re-ran and independently read these structural tests: exactly one executeLoanIssuanceAttempt export, exactly one executeRepaymentClaim/executeDefaultDetectionSweep export each, lending-orchestrator.mjs is the ONLY call site for verifyRepayment/detectDefaultedLoans/reconcileProvisionalDisbursement (grep across skills/economy/lending confirms this independently), and CRIT-204's lock-namespace-crossing regex checks pass. `grep -rln 'reconcileProvisionalDisbursement\|payViaFacilitator\|verifyRepayment\|detectDefaultedLoans' skills/economy/lending/lib/*.mjs` (excluding tests) confirms lending-orchestrator.mjs is the sole production call site for all four.

CRIT-204's dual-lock-vs-single-lock scope separation independently re-verified under REAL concurrent execution (not just the structural grep): PROP-115d's own staggered-race test confirms a concurrent issuance attempt for the SAME lender fails throughout step 9's in-flight window and only succeeds after the first attempt's own lock releases; the adversary's own additional sweep-self-race probe (edge_case_coverage evidence above) independently confirms the per-loan lock never crosses into or interferes with concurrent per-lender/per-borrower-locked issuance activity, since the two lock key namespaces (`loan_${lenderId}`/`loan_borrower_${borrowerId}` vs `loan_${loanId}` where loanId itself always has the form `loan_${lenderId}_${n}`, making the per-loan key literally `loan_loan_${lenderId}_${n}`) are structurally non-overlapping by construction, confirmed by direct string-shape inspection.

CRIT-202 structural read: grepped the full file body for relational/threshold comparisons against a balance/surplus/rate/count value -- the only comparisons present are `lockResult.ok===false`/`disburseResult.ok!==true`/`verifyResult.credited>0`-style outcome checks on already-computed results from called functions, `repaidUsd>=lastRow.total_due_usd`/`nowMs<=lastRow.due_ms` (these mirror REQ-108's own already-specified repayment-completion/on-time comparisons, not a new eligibility/sizing decision), and default-detection candidate-freshness re-checks inside executeDefaultDetectionSweep (status/due_ms/repaid_usd comparisons that are the SAME re-check REQ-109's own detectDefaultedLoans logic already performs, applied here only to confirm a step-1 candidate is still valid at step 2, never a new independent threshold). No LLM/prompt reference found anywhere in the file.
